claim: Deep ensembles and MC Dropout are shown to lack the input-distance-awareness property: their confidence is governed by distance to the decision boundary, not distance to training data, so they assign low uncertainty to OOD points far from training data.
stance_target: N4: deep ensembles are confidently wrong far from the data
quoted_support: deep ensembles (Figures 1b, 1g) and MC Dropout (Figures 1c, 1h) are based on dense output layers that are not distance aware. As a result, both methods quantify their predictive uncertainty based on the distance from the decision boundaries, assigning low uncertainty to OOD examples even if they are far from the data.
